correctness.rationale: The normal basis theorem converts \(x=Mx^{[2]}\) exactly to a cyclic system \(v_j=Mv_{j-1}\), proving a bijection with \(\ker(I-M^f)\). A finite-field-defined Fitting decomposition eliminates the nilpotent part and proves exactly \(2^r\) geometric points and minimal splitting degree \(\operatorname{ord}(M|_U)\). Möbius inversion then gives the zeta function. The standalone bit-exact verifier independently enumerates 530 small binary matrices over three fields and all points in the named graph examples.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Existing definitions, expansion estimates, and partial permutation-family idempotents do not by themselves imply the extension-rank identity or the minimal splitting-degree theorem. value.rationale: This is a complete arithmetic distribution for a motivated full class of finite-field graph evolution algebras, not a small example or pointwise existence check. The exact least field of definition and rational zeta function are intrinsic refinements of idempotent counts. Five-cycle and Petersen instances from the 2026 source have different, explicitly quantified Frobenius orbit profiles; these precise invariants have a plausible role in comparing graph evolution algebras.
